title: Lesson 16. My hero
description: Draw a hero in Paint and write a story about it in Word

questions.prompt: Where do we save the hero drawing?
Put the hero story steps in order
The hero can only be a human.
questions.explain: A robot, a space cat or a dragon too.

questions.prompt: How do you put the hero drawing into Word?
Match the hero question with a sample answer
questions.explain: That brings the hero to life.

questions.text: We drew in ___ and wrote the story in ___.

questions.prompt: The hero drawing will be needed later in Scratch.
questions.explain: It comes alive in the game.

questions.prompt: How do we style the hero's name in the title?

learn.intro: Today you invent your own hero. Remember it — at the end of the course it becomes the hero of your own game!

slides.text: The hero can be anyone: a robot, a superhero, a space cat, a dragon. What is its name? What can it do? Where does it live?

check.prompt: The hero you invent will later star in your game.

slides.text: Draw the hero in Paint **big, on a light background** — easier to put into the game later.

check.prompt: How should you draw the hero for the future game?
check.explain: Easier to put into the game.

slides.text: Open Word: the title is the hero's name, big and centred; Insert → Pictures → "My hero"; 3–4 sentences: who it is, what it can do, where it lives, its friends.
You combined two programs: drew in Paint and wrote the story in Word. That's how real designers work!

check.prompt: Which two programs did we combine today?
check.explain: A Paint drawing in a Word story.
